state: The Can toolchain targets one runtime, Bun 1.4.2, and B1-11 must decode TOML, YAML, JSON5 and JSONL documents into statically typed Can values. All decoding flows through the shared specialization design: each generic call site lowers to a factory built from a CodecSchema describing the expected shape with str, int, float and bool leaves composed into arrays, records, errors and variants. Input arrives as bytes::buffer, parsing and projection obey the standaloneBytes byte cap with maxDepth and maxNodes guards, and any mismatch surfaces as codec::invalid_data carrying a path plus a reason like missing_member, extra_member, type, integer_token, nonfinite or duplicate_member. The decode_json path keeps exact integers because projection replays the original numeric tokens rather than trusting rounded doubles. Fresh measurements of the candidate native parsers show: Bun.TOML.parse throws a losslessness SyntaxError on 9007199254740993 and a redefinition SyntaxError on repeated keys, whereas Bun.YAML.parse and Bun.JSON5.parse quietly produce 9007199254740992 from 9007199254740993 and let later duplicates win; each parser produces true NaN and Infinity values from its nonfinite literals; TOML dates arrive as Temporal instances (PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainTime, Instant) but YAML dates arrive as ordinary strings; YAML uses 1.2 core typing where yes and on are strings and every null spelling is null, expands merge keys, returns aliased nodes shared by reference, may hand back a cyclic graph for self-referential anchors, and delivers multi-document streams as an array; TOML insists on a table root yet tolerates mixed-type arrays; Bun.JSONL.parse degrades 9007199254740993 to 9007199254740992, tolerates blank lines, CRLF and a missing final newline, tolerates multi-line records, and upon trailing garbage returns just the good prefix without signalling an error or how many bytes it consumed; Bun.JSONL.parseChunk exposes values, read, done and error for stepwise consumption. Binding constraints: only qualified native parsers, never a hand-rolled document grammar; per-format exactness must be declared honestly; duplicate detection is offered solely where the native layer can substantiate it.

naming.instructions: What naming scheme fits the added format decoders?

criteria.codec_prefixed: Retain a single codec namespace where each decoder name carries its format, extending the decode_json pattern to TOML, YAML, JSON5 and JSONL.
criteria.format_domains: Introduce one namespace per format exposing a terse decode verb alongside a streaming JSONL consumer, as the sketch drafts it.
criteria.single_decode: Offer one parameterized decode accepting a format discriminator and the payload, centralizing every format in a single generic entry point.

jsonl_strictness.instructions: What strictness must JSONL decoding guarantee?

criteria.framed_exact: Frame the input into bounded lines and decode each through exact JSON: skip blanks, allow CRLF and missing trailing newline, refuse records split across lines, keep big integers exact, fail truncated tails.
criteria.native_whole: Parse the whole payload with Bun.JSONL.parse: spanning records pass, large integers lose precision, garbage after the last good record goes unreported.
criteria.framed_native: Split records by line yet decode values natively per line: spanning records fail while large integers lose precision anyway.

toml_dates.instructions: Which crossing should TOML date and time values take?

criteria.reject_dates: Treat all Temporal results as non-projectable and raise codec::invalid_data naming the offending path whenever one appears.
criteria.project_instant: Map zoned timestamps onto time::instant values and reject zoneless dates, times and datetimes that no instant can represent.
criteria.project_string: Render each Temporal result as ISO-8601 text and decode it wherever the schema asks for str.
